transcript:
[2026-10-09T18:30:21.130Z] 00:00:00] Maya (Meeting Lead): Good morning, everyone. Let’s get
started. We have five things to cover today: project progress, the
launch budget, marketing, team responsibilities, and a few risks. Please
keep updates brief, and let’s finish with clear action items.

[00:00:18] Arun (Developer): The dashboard is about seventy percent
complete. The main pages are working, and the meeting summary panel is
connected to the test data. I still need to improve the loading state
and handle cases where the transcript is empty.

[00:00:34] Maya: Is the current timeline still realistic?

[00:00:37] Arun: Yes, if we finish testing by Thursday. I can complete
the loading state tomorrow and ask Priya to test the empty-transcript
case. The larger issue is that live updates sometimes arrive twice, so I
want to check the WebSocket event handling before we call it ready.

[00:00:57] Priya (QA): I’ll prepare a short test checklist today. It
will cover connecting, sending transcript text, receiving an update,
resetting a meeting, and checking that the summary is saved. I’ll also
test a long transcript with several topics.

[00:01:16] Maya: Great. Let’s move to the budget. Finance has approved
the current development budget, but we have very little room for extra
cloud services. We should avoid adding paid tools unless they solve a
clear problem.

[00:01:31] Daniel (Finance): Correct. The current estimate covers
development and basic testing. If we need additional hosting, we should
compare the monthly cost before choosing a provider. Please send me the
expected usage and storage requirements by Wednesday.

[00:01:47] Maya: Decision: we won’t add a new paid service this week.
Daniel will review the hosting options after receiving the estimates.

[00:01:58] Leena (Marketing): For marketing, I suggest a small
demonstration video showing how a meeting transcript becomes short
summary points. We can also prepare a one-page overview for people who
want to understand the product quickly.

[00:02:13] Maya: Who is the main audience?

[00:02:16] Leena: Student project teams and small organizations that
have frequent discussions and need a quick record of decisions. We
should focus the message on saving time and making action items easier
to find, rather than promising perfect transcription.

[00:02:33] Arun: We should make sure the demo uses fictional meeting
data. We shouldn’t display real meeting transcripts or personal details.

[00:02:42] Leena: Agreed. I’ll draft the overview and video outline by
Friday. Once the dashboard is stable, we can record the demo.

[00:02:55] Maya: Next, responsibilities. We have overlapping work on
testing and documentation. Priya will own the test checklist. Arun will
handle the dashboard fixes and WebSocket issue. Leena will prepare the
marketing materials. Daniel will review the hosting costs. I’ll combine
the final status into one project update.

[00:03:16] Priya: One concern: we don’t yet have a clear process for
reporting bugs. I suggest a shared issue list with a title, steps to
reproduce, expected result, actual result, and priority.

[00:03:30] Maya: Good idea. Decision: use a shared issue list for
testing. Priya can create it today, and everyone should add problems
there instead of sending them in separate messages.

[00:03:42] Daniel: There is also a schedule risk. If the WebSocket
problem takes longer than expected, the demo recording could slip. Could
we prepare a backup using a saved transcript?

[00:03:54] Arun: Yes. We can keep a sample transcript ready and use it
to demonstrate the analysis flow if live input fails. That won’t replace
fixing the live connection, but it gives us a fallback for the
presentation.

[00:04:08] Maya: Let’s record that as a risk and mitigation: live
updates may be unstable, so we will prepare a saved-transcript fallback
while still testing the real-time path.

[00:04:21] Leena: Before we close, can we agree on the launch message? I
recommend saying the tool organizes discussion into topics, short
summaries, and action items. We should clearly state that users need to
review the generated notes for accuracy.

[00:04:37] Maya: Agreed. We’ll describe it as an assistant for meeting
notes, not as a replacement for human review.

[00:04:47] Priya: Quick recap: I’ll create the test checklist and shared
issue list today. Arun will fix loading and duplicate-update issues,
then test the transcript flow. Daniel needs usage estimates by
Wednesday. Leena will deliver the overview and demo outline by Friday.

[00:05:03] Maya: Thanks, everyone. Our target is to finish the main
fixes and testing by Thursday, review the marketing materials on Friday,
and decide whether we’re ready for the demo at our next meeting. Please
update the issue list as you complete tasks. Meeting closed.
meeting_summary: Project progress, budget, marketing, responsibilities, risks, and launch messaging were discussed with action items set for each area.
